newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN panel to review Iran-Iraq smuggling Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: UN panel to review Iran-Iraq smuggling Tuesday.

text.p: Charges made four months ago by the United States accusing Iran of allowing contraband shipments of Iraqi gasoil to pass through Iranian waters will be reviewed Tuesday by the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq.
Leading delegates on the panel said the review of U.S. charges was not related to the implementation of the oil-for-food deal between Iraq and the United Nations.
"This has nothing to do with that (oil-for-food)," said a diplomat on the sanctions committee.
The United States first accused Iran of aiding illegal gasoil shipments in early August, but had not submitted a written report, which it was slated to do on Tuesday.
A spokesman for the U.S. delegation to the United Nations said the report was an effort to get committee action against the alleged Iranian assistance.
"This is documentation of those charges from August. We will see what can be done. We want the Iranians to be told to stop," said the U.S. spokesman.
Western diplomats said the committee was also scheduled for a briefing from the secretariat on progress in implementing the oil-for-food accord.

Inspectors from Lloyds Register are in Iraq checking on facilities along the Turkey-Iraq border for monitoring aid imports. Separate inspections of oil metering stations were to start Tuesday or Wednesday by teams from the Dutch-firm Saybolt, U.N. officials said.

Once the inspections are satisfactorily completed, all that stands in the way for Iraqi oil exports would be a final report from U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to the Security Council, saying all steps are implemented.
That report could come in the next 5-10 days, according to diplomats and U.N. sources.

Under the oil deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worht of crude over a renewable, six-month period in order to buy food and aid for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed in 1990 after Baghdad invaded Kuwait.
